summary.text: Ramirez has represented Illinois' 3rd Congressional District since January 2023. Before Congress she spent nearly two decades in the nonprofit sector and served two terms in the Illinois House of Representatives (2019-2023), where she co-founded the House Progressive Caucus. She is seeking re-election after an unopposed March 2026 primary.

paragraphs.text: Born in Chicago and, according to her official biography, the daughter of working-class Guatemalan immigrants and a lifelong resident of the Humboldt Park neighborhood.
Earned a bachelor's degree in justice studies from Northeastern Illinois University.

Spent 18 years in nonprofit work, according to her official biography: executive director of the Center for Changing Lives, campaign manager at Common Cause Illinois, and deputy director of Community Renewal Society. Ballotpedia also lists her as a social services administrator, community organizer and policy advocate, and a co-founder of Justice for Our Neighbors (JFON).
Served as board chair of the Latin United Community Housing Association (LUCHA) and the Logan Square Neighborhood Association (LSNA).

Elected in 2018 to the Illinois House of Representatives, 4th District, and served 2019-2023. Her official biography says she co-founded the Illinois House Progressive Caucus, became an Assistant Majority Leader in her second term, and lists among her legislation Medicaid coverage for seniors regardless of immigration status, funding for affordable housing and an elected Chicago school board.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2022 and took office January 3, 2023, succeeding Marie Newman. Her official biography describes her as the first Latina elected to Congress from Illinois and the Midwest.
Serves on the House Committee on Homeland Security and the Committee on Veterans' Affairs, where she is the top Democrat on the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.

Her official biography says she is the only member of Congress in a mixed-status family, is married to Boris, and lives in Chicago. She ran unopposed in the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary (72,443 votes).
